findings.finding: The stock has rebounded about +26% from a $14.78 mid-September level (CFO Form 4 withholding price, 2026-09-20) and $15.03 on 2026-10-07 to $18.99, +11.25% over 20 days per the baseline, while large-cap software (IGV) went from +5.4% YTD on 2026-10-26 to about -5% YTD on 2026-11-10; no company news explains it other than an Oct 9 revolver refinancing, so the real bar into the FY27 guide is higher than the post-August consensus implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last three guide-touching prints sold off -10.54% (Nov 2025 initial FY26 guide), -7.73% (May 2026 cut), -20.45% (Aug 2026 cut); only Feb 2026 rose (+5.27%). Run-up into those prints not sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: A rebound is itself price, but what it implies is not: if the market were still discounting another cut the stock would sit near the $15 September low and short interest would be rising, not down 18%; instead it trades as if the guide reset is done.
findings.independence: Price path from a different source: $15.03 close 2026-10-07 and $17.37 on 2026-10-23 (https://www.foxbusiness.com/quote?stockTicker=IIIV, snippet); sector from https://chartrow.com/quote/igv/trailing-returns. findings.finding: The print delivers the first formal FY27 guide: on the 2026-08-07 call management cut FY27 revenue growth to mid-single digits (~$227-232M on a ~$218.5M FY26 midpoint) with 100-200bp margin expansion and promised more detail in November, after cutting FY26 at both the May and August prints; the CFO said professional-services declines in utilities continue year over year into Q4, so a third downward step is the main risk, while a guide at the flagged level is mostly priced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide events: Nov 2025 initial FY26 guide -10.54%; May 2026 FY26 cut -7.73%; Aug 2026 FY26 cut plus FY27 lowered -20.45%.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's FY27 is not visible post-cut (stale pre-August $239-250M is the only full-year figure found), so whether models sit at mid-single digits or still above is unknown; if the market had priced another cut the stock would not have rebounded +26% while shorts covered.
findings.independence: CFO Q4 professional-services comment and interchange detail from https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/i3-verticals-q3-earnings-call-highlights (same call, so one document family). Stale FY27 consensus https://es.finance.yahoo.com/quote/IIIV/analysis.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 EPS beat ($0.25 vs $0.23) with a revenue miss fell -20.45%; EPS beats have not been paid on this name when the guide moved down.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-09 i3 Verticals replaced its $400M revolver with a $350M JPMorgan-agented senior secured revolver (max net leverage 4.0x, min interest cover 3.0x, accordion up to greater of $100M or 100% LTM EBITDA, general corporate uses); against ~$114M of debt at June and ~$58M of FY26 adj EBITDA (~2x), the money buys refinanced liquidity for the $100M buyback authorised May 2026 and tuck-in M&A, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior financing-led reaction in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Filed as an 8-K with no press release and no analyst coverage found; Q4 buyback volume against the $100M program will only be visible in the release.
findings.independence: $100M buyback authorisation, 2026-05-12 (https://i3verticals.gcs-web.com/static-files/074aad8f-3737-43dd-9956-efd060a7968a, search snippet); balance sheet from the Q3 release.

findings.finding: On the Q3 call management named Q4-specific fixes: more than $1M of the guide cut came from net payment take rates hit by commercial-card interchange, with a processor data fix expected in Q4, and four material statewide transportation services went live, which the CEO said should re-accelerate recurring revenue; both feed Q4 recurring revenue and the FY27 starting rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Recurring/ARR has grown 8-11% every quarter while the stock fell on non-recurring misses; the market has not paid ARR before.
findings.why_not_priced: If the fix and go-lives were credited, FY27 street would sit above mid-single digits; the only FY27 figure visible is management's own lowered one, and the stock remains 35% below its 52-week high.
findings.independence: Go-live quote also in the company release (https://finviz.com/news/379184/i3-verticals-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results); same quarter's disclosures, so not independent of finding 3.

findings.finding: Tyler Technologies (reported 2026-10-28, after i3 last spoke) grew Q3 transaction revenue 9.5% (14.2% ex-Texas) and guided FY26 professional services 0-2%, i.e. state/local payments demand healthy and services flat, not collapsing.
findings.link: Both sell case-management, utility-billing and payment software to US state and local governments (i3: public sector is essentially all continuing revenue; Tyler is the largest vendor in the same buyer set); no shared-customer figure found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of IIIV reacting to Tyler prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy only: i3's own problem was implementation delays on specific utility CIS projects, which a sector read cannot resolve; a market crediting it would have re-rated small public-sector software, and IGV fell instead.

findings.finding: Paymentus (reported 2026-11-02) grew Q3 revenue 19.8% to $372.2M, beat the top of its own guide on revenue and EBITDA, and raised FY26 for the third straight quarter: utility and biller payment volumes were strong in the same quarter i3 reports.
findings.link: Same end market for part of i3's transaction revenue (utility and public-sector bill payments); i3's utilities weakness was professional services, not payment volume, so the overlap is partial; no revenue-share figure found.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy; i3's transaction slowdown was a take-rate (interchange) issue, which volume elsewhere does not settle.

baseline_tension: No skew to read; the +11% 20-day run-up (about +26% off the September low) against a falling software tape cuts against a positive reaction to an in-line guide, while the falling but still large short interest cuts against a strong negative, so the evidence leaves the sign close to balanced with a slight negative lean.
